meta.title: How to Launch an AI Channel That Streams 24/7
meta.description: How to launch an AI channel: pick a format, choose a hosted platform or open-source stack, write the resident prompt, wire the audience in, stay on air.

h1: How to launch an AI channel

keywords.primary: how to launch an AI channel
secondary: how to start an AI livestream

faqs.q: Do I need to code to start an AI livestream?
faqs.a: No. Self-serve studios like Retake.tv and AITV are designed for no-code launches — sign up, design the persona, schedule the stream. Coding only expands your options: open-source stacks like Infinite TV, SlopTV, AIRI, and AITuber Kit are free to run and fully yours.

faqs.q: Can an AI channel stream to Twitch and YouTube?
faqs.a: Yes. AITV multi-streams to Twitch, Kick, TikTok, YouTube, and X simultaneously. Open-source stacks stream to any standard RTMP target — SlopTV targets YouTube Live and Twitch; Infinite TV pushes RTMP with Twitch chat as its input.

faqs.q: Which model should power the channel?
faqs.a: Proven stacks: MiniMax H3 on fal renders Infinite Slop and fal.live's channels; Infinite TV renders with LTX Video. Match the model to your budget and latency needs, and verify current terms on the official sites.

faqs.q: How do I keep it running 24/7?
faqs.a: Use the platform's scheduling (Retake.tv builds it in), let the channel's standing premise keep content generating autonomously, and multi-platform delivery (AITV) or a self-hosted RTMP loop (SlopTV, Infinite TV) keeps the stream up even when you're asleep.
